method: After freezing and replaying the decision, returned to the official major-choice credit table, current course-domain list and bachelor research entry rules and rebuilt the credit allocation from those sources. Rechecked experimental and Python training descriptions against the current UCR workbook and reconsidered statistical, clinical, developmental, cognitive and organizational evidence independently of the published candidate labels. findings: The Dutch-taught Psychology bachelor totals 180 EC: eight first-year courses (60 EC), a bachelor research project (15 EC), major-choice courses (60 EC) and profiling (45 EC). The student major-choice page specifies 15 EC social context, 15 EC theory, 7.5 EC professional skills, 7.5 EC research training, 7.5 EC advanced methods and 7.5 EC free choice within theory, skills or social context. The two trainings divide 7.5 EC equally. The example follows official first-listed thematic and research choices and the first-listed clinical science grouping. It fills the professional-skills slot with interviewing and the remaining free choice with clinical developmental theory. This is a coherent set of electives across categories, not a compulsory specialization or a credential pathway.

The student curriculum places the two thematic courses, both trainings and advanced methods in the first semester of year two. The themes are in different blocks. Theory and interviewing are later choices, with interviewing listed for blocks 3 or 4. The bachelor research page requires completion of introductory, applied and advanced methods before the year-three project. Completing both skills trainings is recommended for projects that use their methods. The project can take either year-three semester. At least 45 EC at level 3 are required across the major and profiling, with sufficient room to meet the requirement. The current OER is linked via the university index, but the document returned a security verification screen. The current official student curriculum, detailed credit rules, domain catalog and research page directly resolve the review questions. The published current errata do not amend Psychology.

The broad plan retains the full psychology sequence across brain, social psychology, development, psychopathology, assessment and health, and uses quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods. Sociology and behavioral economics complement psychological work with institutions and decisions. The brain and cognition plan combines neurobiology, perception, psycholinguistics and higher cognition with physiology, laboratory practice, philosophy of mind and emotion, Python and data methods. Programming and statistics prepare for later computational work. Computer vision teaches image representations and machine vision, which complement study of human perception without supplying neuroscience. The work plan combines social psychology, leadership, stress, negotiation, diversity and behavioral choice with market and qualitative research. AI in business and international governance address organizational context, not core psychology. Clinical and developmental topics already have a credible home in the broad plan. The alternatives cannot support clinical training or a developmental direction at substantially greater depth. Eight positive alignments document shared subject matter or methods. Utrecht’s advanced statistics, interviewing, specialized clinical theory and required research remain distinguishable from UCR coursework.
